title: Prom and Mixtape
premise: Felix Vasquez, Cedar Hollow High's undefeated debate champion, has spent years perfecting the art of not talking about his family — especially his late mother's role in founding the town's beloved Spring Mixtape Prom, a tradition now threatened when the school board votes to cancel it over budget cuts and an old scandal. When his debate teacher pairs him with Priya Chandrasekaran, his academic rival and the school board chair's daughter, for a semester-long civic project, the two are forced to dig into the prom's history and uncover a truth neither expected: Felix's mother and Priya's father were once best friends whose falling-out started the scandal in the first place. As archival tapes, buried letters, and reluctant witnesses pull them closer, Felix and Priya must decide whether loyalty to their families matters more than the truth — and whether saving the prom means exposing what their parents did. In the end, they rebuild the tradition on honest terms, host a prom that honors both families' versions of the past, and admit, somewhere between a slow song and a shared mixtape, that they were never really enemies at all.
about_author: August Voss is the pen name of a former high-school debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers argue brilliantly about everything except themselves. Voss writes small-town YA stories about the inheritances we didn't ask for and the songs that get us through them.

chapters.title: Objection, Your Honor
chapters.summary: Felix Vasquez's POV. Felix wins the regional debate final while dodging texts from his dad about the school board's vote to cancel the Spring Mixtape Prom — the tradition his late mother helped create. At home, the argument he can't win simmers untouched. Emotional beat: polished public confidence masking private fracture.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Priya Chandrasekaran's POV. Ms. Okafor pairs Felix and Priya for a semester-long civic project: document a local tradition worth saving. Priya, whose mother chairs the school board that killed the prom, insists she doesn't care about it. Their first planning session is pure warfare. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, sparks of grudging respect.

chapters.title: Side B of the Story
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Researching in the library basement, they find a 1998 mixtape labeled 'For J.V., always' — Felix's mother's initials — and a newspaper clipping about a prom-night feud between two founding students. One name is redacted; the other is Priya's father. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confronts his dad, who shuts down harder than ever, revealing only that he and Raj Chandrasekaran 'don't talk anymore.' Felix starts interviewing prom alumni behind Priya's back, treating her like an opposing witness. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized into secrecy.

chapters.title: The Rebuttal She Didn't Prepare
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers Felix's solo interviews and feels betrayed, then overhears her own mother dismiss the prom as 'a nostalgia tax.' Caught between camps, she secretly listens to the mixtape and hears her father's young voice laughing with Felix's mom. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under inherited loyalties.

chapters.title: Detention, Duet
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Punished together after a hallway blowup, Felix and Priya actually talk — about grief, pressure, and parents who treat truth like a threat. They agree to finish the project jointly and follow the tape's last clue to a retired teacher who was there in 1998. Emotional beat: truce, tenderness, first real honesty.

chapters.title: What the Tape Won't Say
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The retired teacher reveals the scandal: Raj took credit for the prom idea that was really Felix's mother's, and she let him, hoping friendship would survive. It didn't. Priya realizes her family's legacy is built on Felix's mother's silence. Emotional beat: guilt, and the weight of knowing too much.

chapters.title: Motion to Strike
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Priya confesses everything to Felix before he can hear it elsewhere — a choice her father never made. Furious and heartbroken, Felix must decide whether to expose Raj publicly at the school board's final vote or protect Priya. He drafts both speeches. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as courage; impossible choice.

chapters.title: The Floor Is Open
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. At the board meeting, Felix delivers a speech that tells the whole truth — including his mother's complicity in her own erasure — and proposes restoring the prom under joint stewardship. Raj, confronted publicly, finally apologizes. The board reverses. Emotional beat: truth offered not as a weapon but as a bridge.

chapters.title: Track One
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. The revived Spring Mixtape Prom opens with both families in the gym, a new tape playing songs chosen by this year's students. Felix's dad and Raj share a stiff, real conversation by the punch bowl. Felix asks Priya to dance; she hands him a mixtape labeled 'Track One.' Emotional beat: belonging chosen, inheritance rewritten.
